# Abstract {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"**Purpose:** Box-score indices such as the EuroLeague Performance Index Rating (PIR) are widely used to value players, and decision-support frameworks optimise lineups on such values. We tested whether these indices are biased by player role, whether they predict future lineup performance, and whether lineups optimised on them outperform coaches' own choices. "
f"**Methods:** Nine EuroLeague seasons ({n(A['games'])} games) were analysed. PIR and a related composite index (VAL) per 40 minutes were compared with regularised adjusted plus-minus (RAPM). Role bias was quantified as the variance explained by five data-driven player roles. Predictive validity was assessed out of time (training 2016–2022, test 2023–2024) and within seasons (values from the first half, outcomes in the second half). Integer linear programming selected each team's highest-value five, which was compared with the five players given most minutes in the first half. "
f"**Results:** Role explained {pp(V['eta2']['PIR40'])}% of between-player variance in PIR but {pp(V['eta2']['RAPM'])}% in RAPM, and among players with the same RAPM, role still explained {pp(V['RAPM_kosullu']['PIR40']['kismi_eta2'])}% of the variance in PIR; the pattern persisted after correction for reliability and with roles defined without PIR components. RAPM predicted out-of-time lineup net rating better than PIR and VAL. Within seasons, only RAPM-based lineup value had a confidence interval excluding zero, although differences between measures were not statistically significant. Optimised fives shared about three of five players with the coach's most-used five and did not differ from it in second-half net rating (all paired 95% confidence intervals included zero, spanning about ±4–5 points per 100 possessions). "
f"**Conclusions:** PIR-type indices rate interior roles higher than players with the same on-court impact in other roles and should not be used to compare players across roles; plus-minus-based values are preferable for this purpose. Lineup optimisation on any of these values showed no advantage over coaches' rotations, which should be the benchmark for lineup decision tools.")
```

# Data and code availability {.unnumbered}

All data were obtained from the public EuroLeague application programming interface. Code reproducing every number, table and figure is available at https://github.com/koksalahmet85-svg/sports-science-paper-engine and will be archived with a persistent identifier on acceptance.

# Use of artificial intelligence {.unnumbered}

A generative AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) was used to assist with literature search, programming and language editing. All numerical results were produced by deterministic, version-controlled code; all sources, analyses and interpretations were verified by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content.
